IntroducedBillHeader.Sponsors: Senate Committee on Health & Long-Term Care (originally sponsored by Senators Thibaudeau, Deccio, Keiser and Johnson)

Bill.BriefDescription: Providing a certification exemption for the conduct of blood-drawing procedures by research staff in the homes of research study participants.

BillBody.BillTitle: AN ACT Relating to a certification exemption for the conduct ofblood-drawing procedures by research staff in the homes of researchstudy participants; amending RCW 18.135.040; and adding a new sectionto chapter 18.135 RCW.
BillBody.EnactingClause: BE IT ENACTED BY THE LEGISLATURE OF THE STATE OF WASHINGTON:

BegSecNew.BegSecText: A new section is added to chapter 18.135 RCWto read as follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: This chapter does not prohibit or restrict the performance ofblooddrawing procedures by health care assistants in the residences ofresearch study participants when such procedures have been authorizedby the institutional review board of a comprehensive cancer center ornonprofit degreegranting institution of higher education and areconducted under the general supervision of a physician.

BegSecAmd.BegSecText: RCW 18.135.040 and 1984 c 281 s 3 are each amended to readas follows:

BillSection.RCWSLText: A certification issued to a health care assistant pursuant to thischapter shall be authority to perform only the functions authorized inRCW 18.135.010 subject to proper delegation and supervision in the p. 1 SSB 6690health care facility making the certification or under the supervisionof the certifying health care practitioner in other health carefacilities or in his or her office or in the residences of researchstudy participants in accordance with section 1 of this act. Nocertification made by one health care facility or health carepractitioner is transferrable to another health care facility or healthcare practitioner.
